### dragTo and drag with button selection

Source: https://github.com/asweigart/pyautogui/blob/master/docs/mouse.rst

Shows how to drag the mouse with dragTo() and drag(), including absolute and relative positioning, optional duration, and the button keyword for 'left', 'middle', or 'right' mouse buttons.

```python
>>> pyautogui.dragTo(100, 200, button='left')     # drag mouse to X of 100, Y of 200 while holding down left mouse button
>>> pyautogui.dragTo(300, 400, 2, button='left')  # drag mouse to X of 300, Y of 400 over 2 seconds while holding down left mouse button
>>> pyautogui.drag(30, 0, 2, button='right')   # drag the mouse right 30 pixels over 2 seconds while holding down the right mouse button
```

--------------------------------

### Enable Fail-Safe Mode

Source: https://github.com/asweigart/pyautogui/blob/master/docs/quickstart.rst

Enables fail-safe mode. When True, moving the mouse to the upper-left corner raises a pyautogui.FailSafeException that can abort the program.

```pycon
>>> import pyautogui
>>> pyautogui.FAILSAFE = True
```

--------------------------------

### Take and save a screenshot with pyautogui.screenshot()

Source: https://github.com/asweigart/pyautogui/blob/master/docs/screenshot.rst

Calling screenshot() returns an Image object. Passing a filename string saves the screenshot to that file and returns the Image object. On a 1920x1080 screen, this takes roughly 100 milliseconds.

```python
>>> import pyautogui
>>> im1 = pyautogui.screenshot()
>>> im2 = pyautogui.screenshot('my_screenshot.png')
```

--------------------------------

### Right-click with pyautogui.click(button='right')

Source: https://github.com/asweigart/pyautogui/blob/master/docs/mouse.rst

Performs a right-button click at the current mouse position.

```python
>>> pyautogui.click(button='right')  # right-click the mouse
```

### Fail-Safes

Source: https://github.com/asweigart/pyautogui/blob/master/docs/index.rst

Like the enchanted brooms from the Sorcerer’s Apprentice programmed to keep filling (and then overfilling) the bath with water, a bug in your program could make it go out of control. It’s hard to use the mouse to close a program if the mouse cursor is moving around on its own.

As a safety feature, a fail-safe feature is enabled by default. When a PyAutoGUI function is called, if the mouse is in any of the four corners of the primary monitor, they will raise a `pyautogui.FailSafeException`. There is a one-tenth second delay after calling every PyAutoGUI functions to give the user time to slam the mouse into a corner to trigger the fail safe.

You can disable this failsafe by setting `pyautogui.FAILSAFE = False`. **I HIGHLY RECOMMEND YOU DO NOT DISABLE THE FAILSAFE.**

The tenth-second delay is set by the `pyautogui.PAUSE` setting, which is `0.1` by default. You can change this value. There is also a `pyautogui.DARWIN_CATCH_UP_TIME` setting which adds an additional delay on macOS after keyboard and mouse events, since the operating system appears to need a delay after PyAutoGUI issues these events. It is set to `0.01` by default, adding an additional hundredth-second delay.

### drag(path: Point[] | Promise<Point[]>): Promise<MouseClass>

Source: https://github.com/nut-tree/nut.js/blob/develop/_autodocs/api-reference/mouse.class.md

Presses and holds the left mouse button, moves the mouse along the specified path, then releases the button. The path can be an array of points or a promise resolving to an array of points.

```APIDOC
## drag(path: Point[] | Promise<Point[]>): Promise<MouseClass>

### Description
Presses and holds `Button.LEFT`, moves along `path` via `move()`, then releases the button.

### Method
async

### Signature
```typescript
public async drag(path: Point[] | Promise<Point[]>): Promise<MouseClass>
```

### Parameters
- **path** (`Point[] | Promise<Point[]>`) - Required - The path to drag along, either as an array of points or a promise resolving to an array of points.

### Returns
- **Promise<MouseClass>** - A promise that resolves to the MouseClass instance for chaining.

### Example
```typescript
import { mouse, straightTo, randomPointIn, Region } from "@nut-tree/nut-js";

(async () => {
  const target = new Region(500, 500, 100, 100);
  await mouse.drag(straightTo(randomPointIn(target)));
})();
```

### Source
`mouse.class.ts:209`
```

### Platform-specific native binding selection

Source: https://github.com/nut-tree/nut.js/blob/develop/_autodocs/api-reference/default-providers.md

Selects the appropriate native libnut package based on the current platform (win32, linux, or darwin).

```typescript
const libnut: typeof ln = (process.platform === 'win32') ?
    require("@nut-tree/libnut-win32") :
    (process.platform === 'linux') ?
        require("@nut-tree/libnut-linux") :
        require("@nut-tree/libnut-darwin")
```

--------------------------------

### DefaultKeyboardAction

Source: https://github.com/nut-tree/nut.js/blob/develop/_autodocs/api-reference/default-providers.md

Implements the KeyboardProviderInterface using libnut. Provides methods to type text, click, press, release keys, set keyboard delay, and a key lookup map.

```APIDOC
## DefaultKeyboardAction

### Description
Implements the KeyboardProviderInterface using the libnut native module.

### Methods

#### type(input: string): Promise<void>
- Description: Types the given string via libnut.typeString.
- Parameters: input (string) - The text to type.

#### click(...keys: Key[]): Promise<void>
- Description: Reverses the key array, treats the first as the main key, and the rest as modifiers; calls libnut.keyTap.
- Parameters: keys (Key[]) - Main key and optional modifiers.

#### pressKey(...keys: Key[]): Promise<void>
- Description: Presses keys via libnut.keyToggle(nativeKey, "down", modifiers).
- Parameters: keys (Key[]) - Keys to press.

#### releaseKey(...keys: Key[]): Promise<void>
- Description: Releases keys via libnut.keyToggle(nativeKey, "up", modifiers).
- Parameters: keys (Key[]) - Keys to release.

#### setKeyboardDelay(delay: number): void
- Description: Sets keyboard delay via libnut.setKeyboardDelay.
- Parameters: delay (number) - Delay in milliseconds.

### Static Members
- KeyLookupMap: Map<Key, string | null> - Maps Key enum to native key names.
- keyLookup(key: Key): any - Returns the mapped native key name.
```

### capture()

Source: https://github.com/nut-tree/nut.js/blob/develop/_autodocs/api-reference/screen.class.md

Grabs the whole screen and writes it to disk. Resolves with the generated output path.

```APIDOC
## capture()

### Description
Grabs the whole screen and writes it to disk. Resolves with the generated output **path**.

### Method
capture

### Signature
```typescript
public async capture(
    fileName: string,
    fileFormat: FileType = FileType.PNG,
    filePath: string = cwd(),
    fileNamePrefix: string = "",
    fileNamePostfix: string = ""
): Promise<string>
```

### Parameters
- **fileName** (string) - Required - Basename (extension is derived from `fileFormat`).
- **fileFormat** (FileType) - Optional, default `FileType.PNG` - `FileType.PNG = ".png"` / `FileType.JPG = ".jpg"`.
- **filePath** (string) - Optional, default `cwd()` - Output directory.
- **fileNamePrefix** (string) - Optional, default `""` - Prefixed to the name.
- **fileNamePostfix** (string) - Optional, default `""` - Appended to the name.

### Output Path
Assembled by `generateOutputPath` as `join(path, prefix + name + postfix + type)`.

### Example
```typescript
import { screen, FileType } from "@nut-tree/nut-js";

(async () => {
  const path = await screen.capture("evidence", FileType.PNG, "/tmp", "report-", "-v1");
  console.log(path); // /tmp/report-evidence-v1.png
})();
```

Natural-language instruction for the cua-driver agent to automate a legacy Windows app behind a VPN. Stage input files on the machine first; the driver runs on the Windows machine inside the VPN.

### Verify desktop session with cua-driver call list_apps and list_windows

Source: https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guides/recipes

Commands to verify the driver sees the interactive desktop before automating a legacy Windows app behind a VPN. An empty [] means the driver is outside the interactive desktop; see Windows over SSH.

cua-driver call list_apps
cua-driver call list_windows
```

### Create and use a Space (Python)

Source: https://cua.ai/docs/start-here/your-first-cloud-fleet

Python script that creates a Space on the local machine, runs a command, takes a screenshot, queries Cua Driver for windows, and deletes the Space. The first run pulls the container image, which can take a few minutes. On Apple silicon, `uname` prints `aarch64`.

```python
import asyncio
 
import cua
 
 
async def main():
    spaces = cua.embedded().spaces()
    created = await spaces.create(cua.SpaceCreateOptions())
    space = await spaces.space(created.space.id)
    print("space:", created.space.id)
 
    # Run a command.
    out = await space.bash("uname -sm", None)
    print(out.stdout.strip())
 
    # Take a screenshot.
    shot = await space.screenshot(None)
    with open("space.png", "wb") as f:
        f.write(shot.image)
    print("screenshot: space.png")
 
    # Ask Cua Driver in the Space which windows are open.
    windows = await space.call_tool("list_windows", None, None, None)
    print("driver:", "error" if windows.is_error else "ok")
 
    # Delete the Space. Comment this out to keep it and watch it (step 3).
    await spaces.delete(created.space.id)
 
 
asyncio.run(main())
```

### Automate a legacy Windows app behind a VPN

Source: https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guides/recipes

## Automate a legacy Windows app behind a VPN#
Run Cua Driver on the Windows machine inside the VPN, so the desktop session, app traffic, and files stay there.
Confirm the driver sees the app first:
```
cua-driver call list_apps
cua-driver call list_windows
```

An empty `[]` means the driver is outside the interactive desktop; see Windows over SSH. Stage input files on that machine, then:
```
Open the payroll client, log in with the credentials in C:\creds.txt, create a new employee from new_hire.xlsx, generate the onboarding report, and export it as PDF to the Desktop.
```

### list_space_windows

Source: https://cua.ai/docs/spaces/reference/streams-and-display

## list_space_windows#
List the windows open inside the Space.
The windows a viewer can stream now, from StreamService.ListTargets: on screen, sized, normal app windows (no hidden, minimized or system-UI windows), each with its handle, title, app and bounds.
|   |
---|---
Providers| all (cloud, local, direct, relay)
Platforms| all (macos, windows, linux)
Metering| free
Approval| permission `spaces:list_space_windows`, in `spaces:readonly`; read-only, idempotent
Requires (spacesd)| `windows`
Swift SDK| `Space.windows()`
Rust| `Streams::windows`

### Parameters

Parameter| Type| Default| Description
---|---|---|---
`app_name`| `string`| none| Only windows of this app (case-insensitive substring).
`space`| `string`| required| Space id or name.

### Result

JSON: an array of windows (`window_id`, `epoch`, `title`, `app_name`, `app_id`, `pid`, `bounds`, `on_screen`, `focused`, `available`, `limitation`).

### Errors

`invalid_argument`, `not_found`, `ambiguous_sandbox`, `spacesd_not_available`, `capability_missing`
